definition: Two or more linear equations in the same unknowns, solved together, where a solution makes every equation true at once; in IB AI exams a system has up to $3$ unknowns and always exactly one solution.
A sum of terms $ax^{n}$, where each coefficient $a$ is a constant and each power $n$ is a whole number $0, 1, 2, \ldots$; the highest power with a non-zero coefficient is its degree.
A value of the unknown that makes an equation true; the roots of $f(x) = 0$ are the zeros of $f$.
A value $a$ with $f(a) = 0$: the $x$-coordinate of a point where the graph of $y = f(x)$ meets the $x$-axis. The $y$-intercept is a zero only if the graph passes through the origin.
